desc:
Shopify app maintenance and API updates keep an existing app working as Shopify moves forward. Ecom Swift LLC runs a one-time sprint that updates your API version and dependencies, fixes open bugs, checks webhooks and billing, and delivers a health report.

## Why does a Shopify app need maintenance?

A Shopify app needs maintenance because the platform around it keeps changing. Shopify publishes a new API version every quarter and retires older ones after a set period. Packages the app depends on release security fixes. Runtimes reach end of life. An app that is left alone does not stay the same; it slowly drifts out of step until something stops working.

## What happens when updates are skipped

Failures from neglect tend to arrive suddenly. A retired API version starts returning errors. A webhook subscription fails silently, so merchants stop receiving updates. A package with a known weakness sits in the code for months. A billing flow that worked last year breaks on a changed response.

Merchants do not see the cause. They see an app that stopped working, and they leave a poor review or uninstall. Maintenance replaces these surprises with planned, small changes made while nothing is on fire.

## How regular upkeep protects installs

An app that runs cleanly keeps its paying merchants. Stable webhooks mean orders and customers are processed correctly. A working install flow means new merchants can start. Error alerts mean you hear about a problem before a merchant writes in.

There is also a cost side. Updating one API version is a small job. Updating across several versions at once is a large one, because more behavior has changed. Regular sprints keep each jump short.

## What a maintenance sprint covers

- Update to an API version that Shopify currently supports.
- Review of deprecated calls and the replacements they need.
- Dependency updates, ordered so that small safe ones go first.
- Runtime and framework upgrades where the app is far behind.
- Webhook delivery check, including the mandatory privacy topics.
- Billing and install flow test on a development store.
- Error log review, to find repeating failures.
- Bug fixes for the issues you have listed.
- Uptime and error alerts, database backup check and a short written health report.

## How we run the sprint

We start with the health check: which API version the app calls, which packages are outdated, what the logs show and which bugs are open. We then update in small steps, running the install, uninstall and billing paths after each change so a failure points to its cause.

The Basic package updates the API version and reports on health. Standard adds more package updates, a few bug fixes, a log review and a check against App Store requirements. Premium adds a runtime upgrade, more fixes, monitoring and a six-month upkeep plan. This is a one-time sprint, not a monthly plan. If you want ongoing watching, that is quoted separately.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List known bugs before we start, with steps to reproduce them.
- Keep a recent backup of the database.
- Tell us which features matter most to paying merchants.
- Schedule maintenance before a deprecation deadline, not after it.

**Avoid:**
- Updating everything in one day with no test store.
- Ignoring deprecation warnings in the logs.
- Running updates directly on production first.
- Treating maintenance as optional because the app seems fine.

## Who this service is for

Owners of apps that have not been touched for a long time. Teams whose original developer left. Agencies that inherited an app after a Shopify change broke something and need it fixed and stabilized.

## What we need from you

Repository access, collaborator access in your Partner Dashboard, a development store and read access to your error logs. We do not need access to your servers; you can deploy the changes yourself or share deployment access as a limited user. We never ask for passwords.
